case_summary.summary: Reviewer accepted the missing material-to-temperature link and the vapor-phase redundancy cleanup, but rejected deleting the liquid-phase condition and its edge because cross-type redundancy with events was not considered established.

planning_patterns.proposed_change: Add a material-to-temperature edge from the solvent mixture to the high-temperature condition.
planning_patterns.matched_rule: Add a local entity-to-condition link when a retained state node lacks attachment to the material it describes.
planning_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: If a retained condition is causally used but locally unattached, add the missing descriptive link.

planning_patterns.reviewer_reason: Redundancy cannot be identified accross different types
planning_patterns.matched_rule: Do not remove a condition as redundant solely because a related event exists; redundancy requires no independent local causal role, and cross-type semantics are not automatically duplicates.
planning_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Before deleting a state node for redundancy, confirm true functional duplication rather than overlap with an event of a different type.

planning_patterns.matched_rule: Delete a condition node when it adds no independent local causal role beyond the existing event chain.
planning_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Remove a state node when it only restates phase information already carried by explicit release and dispersion events.

planning_patterns.reviewer_reason: Redundancy cannot be identified accross different types
planning_patterns.matched_rule: Do not delete a descriptive edge when the connected condition is retained and cross-type redundancy has not been established.
planning_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Keep a supporting descriptive edge when the underlying state node is still considered valid.

planning_patterns.matched_rule: Delete an edge that only supports a redundant node being removed.
planning_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: When a node is correctly removed as redundant, remove its sole supporting attachment edge as follow-on cleanup.

diagnosis_patterns.observed_pattern: A retained temperature condition was causally active but unattached to its material.
diagnosis_patterns.diagnosis_interpretation: This should be diagnosed as a missing local descriptive link in state attribution, not as a gap in the main accident pathway.
diagnosis_patterns.supporting_rule: A retained material condition that enables an event should still be linked to the material whose state it describes.
diagnosis_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Diagnose unattached retained condition nodes as local-link omissions.

diagnosis_patterns.observed_pattern: An upstream phase condition was kept despite overlap with a related event.
diagnosis_patterns.diagnosis_interpretation: The issue should not be framed as simple redundancy when a condition and an event are different semantic types and duplicate function has not been shown.
diagnosis_patterns.supporting_rule: Redundancy should be diagnosed only when a node lacks an independent local causal role, not merely because a nearby event expresses related meaning.
diagnosis_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Diagnose redundancy by functional duplication, not by condition-event similarity alone.

diagnosis_patterns.observed_pattern: A downstream phase label duplicated meaning already carried by the event sequence.
diagnosis_patterns.diagnosis_interpretation: The issue is appropriately framed as node redundancy because the phase meaning is already captured by the boil, release, and accumulation pathway.
diagnosis_patterns.supporting_rule: If a condition does not contribute an independent local causal role beyond the existing event chain, diagnose it as redundant.
diagnosis_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Diagnose downstream phase labels as redundant when the event chain already fully expresses that state.

diagnosis_patterns.observed_pattern: A descriptive attachment to a retained state node was preserved.
diagnosis_patterns.diagnosis_interpretation: This suggests the diagnosis should not treat the edge as clutter, because the underlying condition was not accepted as redundant.
diagnosis_patterns.supporting_rule: Do not diagnose a descriptive attachment as redundant when the connected state remains a distinct retained description.
diagnosis_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: If the node stays, its basic entity-to-condition attachment usually stays as well.

diagnosis_patterns.observed_pattern: An attachment edge disappeared together with a redundant downstream phase node.
diagnosis_patterns.diagnosis_interpretation: The edge issue is derivative of the node-level redundancy diagnosis rather than a separate structural defect.
diagnosis_patterns.supporting_rule: When a node is diagnosed as redundant, an edge that only serves that node is also redundant.
diagnosis_patterns.few_shot_takeaway: Treat edge cleanup as secondary to the underlying node redundancy diagnosis.

coverage_notes: Acceptance of the vapor-phase node deletion implicitly covered deletion of its only descriptive edge.
Rejection of the liquid-phase node deletion also implied rejection of deleting its supporting descriptive edge.
The accepted material-to-temperature edge addition repaired the retained high-temperature condition after the phase-node review split outcome.
UPDATED_CAUSAL_GRAPH_JSON contains an extra added edge from the liquid-phase condition to the boiling event that was not part of the mapped reviewed suggestions.
